artists.biography:
Porcupine Tree are a rock band formed by Steven Wilson in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, England. Their music is associated with both psychedelic rock and progressive rock, yet having been influenced by trance, krautrock and ambient due to Steven Wilson and Richard Barbieri's penchant for the Kosmische Musik scene of the early 1970s, led by bands such as Tangerine Dream, Neu! and Can. Since the early 2000s (decade), their music has been leaning towards progressive metal and alternative rock.
The band is noted for its multimedia approach, with its live performances including screens displaying a different film projection to each song. This visual element was introduced during the tour for the In Absentia album, when the band started to work with Danish photographer and filmmaker Lasse Hoile. This involvement created a distinctive image for the band.
Despite being signed to both Roadrunner and Atlantic labels, the band has their own record label, Transmission, which they use to launch some independent releases and special editions of their albums. In 2007 the band was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Surround Sound Album with their album Fear of a Blank Planet and then again in 2010 with The Incident.
Music Radar website placed them amongst "The 30 greatest live acts in the world today" (as of 2010), coming at number 4.

perplexity.description:
Staircase Infinities is a brief but essential Porcupine Tree release that bridges the band’s early psychedelic and space-rock phase with the more developed sound of Up the Downstair. Issued in 1994 as a limited EP on Lazy Eye, it gathers leftovers from those sessions alongside a reworked version of the older “Yellow Hedgerow Dreamscape,” giving the set a strong “missing chapter” feel rather than that of a mere odds-and-ends collection.

Musically, the record leans heavily into drifting electronic textures, hazy ambience, and slow-blooming guitar passages, with the rock elements serving the atmosphere more than driving the songs forward. Its reputation rests on how well these pieces extend the mood and ideas of Up the Downstair, especially in the more expansive, kosmische-influenced writing that would later become central to Porcupine Tree’s identity.
